units.title: Unit 4: Nouns: Singular, Plural and Countability
units.objective: Form common plurals and distinguish countable and uncountable meanings in everyday adult communication.

lessons.title: Lesson 4.1: Regular and Irregular Plurals
lessons.explanation_en: Plural count nouns usually refer to more than one item. Most add -s. Many nouns ending in s, sh, ch, x or z add -es; nouns ending in consonant + y usually change y to -ies. Spellings have exceptions: check unfamiliar words. Learn irregular plurals individually: woman/women, child/children, analysis/analyses, crisis/crises, criterion/criteria. Some nouns, such as sheep and series, have the same singular and plural form. Scissors and trousers normally take plural agreement; a pair of scissors refers to one complete item, and two pairs refers to two items.
lessons.clarification_ar: الجمع يدل عادةً على أكثر من عنصر. نضيف غالبًا s أو es، ونحوّل y إلى ies بعد حرف ساكن. احفظ الجمع الشاذ مثل woman/women وcriterion/criteria؛ ولا تعمم قاعدة واحدة على كل الكلمات. نقول a pair of scissors لأداة مقص كاملة وtwo pairs لأداتين.
lessons.form: Most nouns: +s | Many s/sh/ch/x/z endings: +es | Consonant+y: -ies | Irregular examples: woman/women; criterion/criteria | a pair of scissors
examples: A pair of scissors is in the drawer.
common_mistakes: Use children and women, not childrens and womens, for ordinary plurals.
For one complete cutting tool, use a pair of scissors rather than a scissors.
Criterion has the plural criteria; do not add -s to criteria.

lessons.title: Lesson 4.2: Countable and Uncountable Nouns
lessons.explanation_en: Countable uses refer to separate items and allow singular and plural forms: a report, two reports. In their ordinary mass meanings, advice, information, equipment, furniture and progress are uncountable, take singular agreement and do not combine directly with a/an or a number. Use a piece of advice, three pieces of equipment or three reams of paper to specify amounts. Many and a few go with plural count nouns; much and a little go with uncountable nouns. Some and a lot of can go with either. Much is common in negatives and questions; a lot of is usually more natural in ordinary affirmative statements. Countability can change with meaning: paper as material, a paper as an article; water as a substance, a water as a serving in a suitable ordering context.
lessons.clarification_ar: الأسماء المعدودة لها مفرد وجمع. في معانيها المعتادة لا نجمع advice وinformation وequipment ولا نضع قبلها a/an مباشرة. نقول a piece of advice أوthree pieces of equipment. نستخدم many مع الجمع المعدود وmuch مع غير المعدود، وغالبًا a lot of في الإثبات العادي. قد يتغير العدّ بتغير المعنى؛ a water قد تعني حصة ماء عند الطلب.
lessons.form: Countable: a report / two reports | Uncountable: information is useful | Amounts: a piece of advice / three pieces of equipment | many reports / much information
examples: We ordered three pieces of equipment.
There was not much progress yesterday.
We received a lot of information about the project.
common_mistakes: Use information and equipment without a plural -s in their ordinary mass meanings.
Use advice or a piece of advice, not an advice.
Do not assume that a noun has the same countability in every meaning.

units.title: Unit 5: Articles: A, An, The and No Article
units.objective: Choose articles by sound and distinguish general from identifiable reference in clear contexts.

lessons.title: Lesson 5.1: A or An — Follow the Sound
lessons.explanation_en: Use a or an with a singular count noun when introducing an unspecified example. Choose by the initial sound of the following spoken word, including any adjective: a university and a European company start with /j/, while an hour and an honest answer start with a vowel sound because h is silent. MBA starts with the spoken letter name M, /em/, so use an MBA. Letter names can vary between speakers; a question about H should specify its pronunciation. A/an does not directly modify a plural noun or a noun used in an uncountable meaning. A serving meaning, such as a water in an order, is a different countable use.
lessons.clarification_ar: نختار a أوan حسب أول صوت في الكلمة التالية، بما فيها الصفة، وليس حسب أول حرف مكتوب. نقول a university وa European company لأن الصوت الأول /j/، وan hour وan honest answer لأن h صامت. لا نضعهما قبل جمع أو معنى غير معدود؛ أما الحصة مثل a water في طلب مشروب فهي استعمال معدود مختلف.
lessons.form: a + consonant sound: a university / a European company | an + vowel sound: an hour / an honest answer / an MBA
examples: He earned an MBA at a European university.
We waited for an hour before the interview.
common_mistakes: Choose by sound: an hour and a university.
Use a/an with a singular countable meaning; servings can make an otherwise mass noun countable.

lessons.title: Lesson 5.2: The or No Article — General and Specific Reference
lessons.explanation_en: Use the when the intended referent is identifiable in context, for example because it was mentioned before or both people know which item is meant. Plural count nouns and uncountable nouns often take no article when used generally: Engineers solve problems; water is essential. Compare water in general with the water in this pitcher, when referring to all the identifiable water there. A following phrase does not automatically require the: Engineers who design bridges need training can still describe a group generally. Languages and subjects normally take no article in ordinary uses. Proper names and other patterns have exceptions beyond this lesson. The symbol Ø marks an omitted article in exercises; it is not a word to insert in ordinary writing.
lessons.clarification_ar: نستخدم the عندما يكون المقصود محددًا ويمكن معرفته من السياق. عند التعميم نترك الأداة مع الجمع المعدود وغير المعدود: Engineers solve problems وWater is essential. هذا هو Zero Article ورمزه Ø في التمارين فقط. وجود وصف بعد الاسم لا يفرض the تلقائيًا؛ المهم هل المرجع محدد أم عام.
lessons.form: the + identifiable noun | No article + generic plural or uncountable noun | Ø is an exercise symbol, not a written word
examples: Water is essential for health. The water in this pitcher is filtered.
The engineers who designed our prototype are here for the meeting.
Engineers who design bridges need specialist training.
She studies economics and speaks French.
common_mistakes: For the general concept, write Life is beautiful, without the.
Do not treat every modifying phrase as proof that the is required.
Do not insert the symbol Ø into normal sentences.

questions.prompt: Which sentence talks about coffee generally, then about the particular coffee in the speaker's cup?
options: The coffee is a popular beverage, but coffee in my cup is cold.
Coffee is a popular beverage, but the coffee in my cup is cold.
A coffee is a popular beverage, but a coffee in my cup is cold.

accepted_answers: Coffee is a popular beverage, but the coffee in my cup is cold.
questions.explanation: Coffee has no article for the general beverage. The coffee in my cup identifies the particular coffee being discussed.

writing_tasks.prompt: Write a professional supply request memo (60–90 words) to your office administrator. Include at least two plural count nouns, two uncountable nouns with suitable partitives or quantifiers, and examples of a/an and the where appropriate.
writing_tasks.model_response:
Dear Sarah,

I am writing to request additional office supplies for our department. We need a new printer for the main office and two pairs of scissors for the design team. In addition, please order three reams of paper and a box of pens. We also require some advice regarding the delivery schedule for the new computer equipment. Thank you for your assistance with this matter.

Best regards,
Mark
review_criteria: Check ordinary plural forms, including supplies, pairs and pens.
Use suitable amounts with uncountable nouns, such as three reams of paper and some advice.
Choose a/an by sound and the for identifiable references.
Aim for 60–90 words and a clear professional request. Word count alone does not measure writing quality.
